summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old woman with a history of coronary artery disease, prior CABG, diabetes, hypertension, and asthma was admitted for worsening shortness of breath and productive cough over one week, associated with pleuritic chest pain and recent high salt intake. Evaluation revealed no evidence of pneumonia, pulmonary embolism, or acute myocardial infarction. Her symptoms were attributed to an acute exacerbation of diastolic heart failure, likely precipitated by dietary salt overload, along with acute bronchitis. She was treated with intravenous furosemide, which improved her respiratory status, and continued on her baseline cardiac, pulmonary, and diabetes medications. Her blood glucose improved with insulin therapy, and she was discharged home in stable condition with no medication changes and instructions to follow up with primary care and cardiology.
